I'll search for information about altavista.com for you.

<tool>web_search</tool>
<query>altavista.com history search engine</query>

Based on my search, here's information about **altavista.com**:

AltaVista was one of the most significant early web search engines, launched in **1995** by Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC). It was created by researchers at DEC's Western Research Laboratory, with the name meaning "a view from above" in Spanish.

## Key Historical Points:

- **1995**: Launched as one of the first full-text search engines on the web
- **1998**: Acquired by Compaq when it purchased DEC
- **1999**: Sold to CMGI, an Internet investment company
- **2003**: Acquired by Overture Services, which was then bought by Yahoo! the same year
- **2013**: Yahoo! officially shut down AltaVista on July 8, 2013

## Technical Significance:

AltaVista was groundbreaking for its time, offering:
- Fast, full-text indexing of web pages
- Advanced search syntax (Boolean operators, phrase searching)
- Multilingual search capabilities
- One of the largest indexes of web pages in the 1990s

At its peak in the late 1990s, AltaVista was one of the most popular search engines, though it eventually lost market share to Google, which launched in 1998. The domain altavista.com now redirects to Yahoo's search page.

Sources:
1. https://www.britannica.com/topic/AltaVista
2. https://www.computerhistory.org/timeline/search-engines/
